transcript: Recently I learned how to use our product analytics tool properly, which sounds small but it changed how I work. Before, I only knew a customer was unhappy when they complained or didn't renew, which is way too late. I noticed our data team had usage dashboards that nobody in customer success looked at. So I asked one of the analysts, Long, if he'd spend an hour a week with me for a month, and in exchange I'd tell him what customers actually asked about. He agreed. I learned how to build a simple view, logins per week, features used, and, um, how many seats were active versus paid for. Then I made a basic health list for my forty accounts, red, amber, green. The first month I called the six red ones before their renewal. Four of them had something we could fix, mostly nobody trained on a new feature. All four renewed. The quarter before, I'd lost three accounts that looked exactly like that. My team lead asked me to show it to the others, and now three of us use the same list.
